description: The line plot illustrates the relative change in performance across different layers for four distinct token-precision configurations used in KV cache compression, with the x-axis representing four layer ranges—Layer1-4, Layer5-12, Layer13-20, and Layer29-32—and the y-axis showing the relative change in percentage, ranging from -15% to 5%. The data points are connected by lines, each corresponding to a specific configuration: "LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit" (yellow line with circular markers), "LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit" (red line with square markers), "RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit" (light blue line with circular markers), and "RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit" (dark blue line with square markers). The "LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit" configuration starts at approximately 0% relative change in Layer1-4, dips to around -1% in Layer5-12, rises to about -0.5% in Layer13-20, and ends at approximately 0.5% in Layer29-32. The "LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit" configuration begins at around 0.5% in Layer1-4, decreases to about -1% in Layer5-12, remains stable at approximately -1% in Layer13-20, and ends at around 0.5% in Layer29-32. The "RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit" configuration starts at approximately 0% in Layer1-4, drops to around -5% in Layer5-12, further decreases to about -6% in Layer13-20, and then rises to approximately -1% in Layer29-32. The "RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit" configuration begins at around -1% in Layer1-4, decreases to approximately -5% in Layer5-12, drops sharply to about -14% in Layer13-20, and then rises to approximately -2% in Layer29-32. The plot includes a dashed gray line at 0% relative change, serving as a reference point for performance stability.
